metais unpack — Write a packed package's source directory, to edit it.

Usage:
  metais unpack <package> --to <dir> [--dry-run] [--limit <name>=<value>]...
                [--json]

Writes every entry of the packed package into <dir>, as the source directory it
was packed from: the manifest as its author wrote it, the inputs, templates,
references, assets and examples. .compiled/ is not written: it is derived from
the rest, and metais pack writes it again. Files are written with mode 0644 and
directories 0755, less the umask, whatever the package records.

Before it writes anything, unpack verifies the whole package as inspect does,
its digests included, and refuses a package that fails, writing nothing. It does
not run check: a package with check errors is the one an author needs to unpack
and fix. A source directory is refused: it is already what unpack would write.

--to is required. A <dir> that does not exist is created, with its missing
parents, by writing beside it and renaming the whole directory into place, so a
failed write leaves nothing. An existing <dir> must be empty, apart from names
beginning with . (such as .git) other than .compiled, and files ending .metais;
it is written in place, and a failed write stops unpack, which lists the files
it wrote and removes none of them. There is no --overwrite: a file left from an
earlier tree would join the unpacked source and be packed with it.

--dry-run lists the files unpack would write, and writes nothing anywhere. It is
refused exactly when unpack would be refused before writing, with the same
findings: a package that fails to open, a source directory, a <dir> that is not
empty or not a directory, and a staging directory left beside a <dir> that does
not exist. What only writing finds out, such as a full disk, it cannot report.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file; - is refused, since a package is read with random
      access. Required.

Flags:
  --to <dir>
      The directory to write the source directory into: one that does not exist
      yet, or an empty one. Required.
  --dry-run
      List the files unpack would write, and write nothing.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  The files written, or with --dry-run that would be, relative to <dir>, in the
  order written. With --json, one metais.unpack/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits

  usage.not_a_packed_package
      The package operand is a source directory, which is already what unpack
      writes.
      Next: metais inspect <package>
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais unpack --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais unpack --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais unpack --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais unpack --help

Examples:
  metais unpack report-1.0.0.metais --to report
      Writes the package's source directory into the new directory report.
  metais unpack report-1.0.0.metais --to . --json
      Writes it into the current directory, which must be empty, and lists the
      files as one metais.unpack/1 document.
  metais unpack report-1.0.0.metais --to report --dry-run
      Lists the files it would write into report, and writes nothing.
